---
title: "order() refuses to sort a whole data.frame"
ref: DF-06
categories: [Data frames and lists]
impact: cryptique
extrait: 'order(data.frame(x = 2:1))'
attendu: "the rows sorted by name, then by n"
versions: "Error since R 4.3.0, a mere warning before"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2024)"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
tab <- data.frame(name = c("b", "a", "b"), n = c(2, 3, 1))
tab[order(tab), ]
```
:::

Pick **R 4.1.3** in the menu: you get a mere warning, and a result that makes no sense.

## Why

`order()` sorts vectors, passed to it one at a time: `order(x, y)` sorts by `x`, then breaks ties by `y`. A data.frame is not a vector. To rank it, `order()` calls `xtfrm()`, whose data.frame method stops with `cannot xtfrm data frames`. The message does not say what to do instead.

Before R 4.3.0, the same method only emitted a warning and ranked all the values of the table laid end to end. You got more indices than rows, and `NA` rows in the result.

## The fix

Pass the columns to `order()` one by one, by hand or with `do.call()`. `unname()` prevents a column named like an argument of `order()` (`decreasing`, `method`) from being taken for it.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
tab[order(tab$name, tab$n), ]
tab[do.call(order, unname(tab)), ]
```
:::
